outline: Functional closure of the foramen ovale
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Normal functional closure of the foramen ovale after birth
mechanism: With the first breaths, pulmonary vascular resistance falls and pulmonary blood flow increases. Increased pulmonary venous return raises left-atrial pressure above right-atrial pressure, pressing the septum primum against the septum secundum and functionally closing the foramen ovale.
vignette: A healthy term newborn takes the first several breaths after delivery. Pulmonary blood flow rapidly increases, and a normal fetal interatrial shunt functionally closes.
lead: Which of the following hemodynamic changes most directly causes this closure?
correct: A fall in pulmonary vascular resistance that increases pulmonary venous return and raises left-atrial pressure above right-atrial pressure
distractors: An increase in pulmonary vascular resistance that raises right-atrial pressure above left-atrial pressure
An increase in arterial oxygen tension that constricts the ductus arteriosus
Continued umbilical venous return that raises right-atrial preload after placental separation
A fall in systemic vascular resistance caused by removal of the placental circulation
distractor_notes: Pulmonary vascular resistance falls after lung expansion; raising right-atrial pressure would favor persistent right-to-left shunting rather than foramen-ovale closure.

Higher oxygen tension after birth contributes to ductus-arteriosus constriction, but the foramen ovale closes because left-atrial pressure rises above right-atrial pressure after pulmonary vascular resistance falls.
Umbilical venous return stops after cord clamping rather than continuing to raise right-atrial preload.
Removal of the low-resistance placenta increases systemic vascular resistance; it does not cause a fall in systemic resistance.
key_expl: The first breaths expand the lungs and sharply reduce pulmonary vascular resistance. Pulmonary blood flow and pulmonary venous return to the left atrium therefore rise, while loss of placental venous return lowers right-sided filling. Once left-atrial pressure exceeds right-atrial pressure, the septum primum is pressed against the septum secundum, producing functional closure of the foramen ovale.
objective: Explain functional closure of the foramen ovale as a consequence of the postnatal fall in pulmonary vascular resistance and rise of left-atrial pressure above right-atrial pressure.
